questions.question: Which keyword is used to exclude a field from serialization?
options: exclude
transient
volatile
static
explanations: exclude is not a Java keyword.
Correct. transient indicates that the field MUST NOT be serialized and will keep its default value when deserialized.
volatile ensures visibility between threads, it does not affect serialization.
static belongs to the class, not to the instance, and it is not serialized anyway.

questions.question: How does serialization work with inheritance?
options: Only the child class is serialized
The entire class hierarchy is serialized if all classes implement Serializable
You must implement writeObject() in each parent class
Java does not allow serializing classes that inherit from others
explanations: Not only the child class is serialized; it includes the fields of the parent classes.
Correct. Serialization includes all fields of the entire class hierarchy, as long as every class in the chain implements Serializable.
writeObject() is optional and not required in every parent class.
Java does allow serializing classes that inherit from others.

questions.question: What is custom serialization?
options: Serializing only the static fields
Implementing writeObject() and readObject() to control what is saved and how
Using an external library to serialize
Serializing only the first half of the object
explanations: Static fields are not serialized anyway.
Correct. By implementing writeObject() and readObject() in the class, you can control exactly which fields are saved and how they are transformed.
Custom serialization does not require external libraries.
It has nothing to do with splitting the object into parts.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using JSON over Java's native serialization?
options: JSON is faster than Serializable
JSON is portable across languages, Serializable only works in Java
JSON can serialize objects without implementing an interface
JSON does not require external libraries
explanations: Speed is not necessarily the main advantage.
Correct. JSON is a readable, portable text format that can be read from any programming language, while Java's native serialization can only be deserialized in Java.
JSON also requires configuration or an interface in many cases.
JSON does require libraries such as Gson, Jackson, or similar.

questions.question: How do you deserialize an object in Java?
options: ObjectOutputStream.readObject()
ObjectInputStream.readObject()
ObjectDeserializer.deserialize()
File.readObject()
explanations: ObjectOutputStream writes objects, it does not read them.
Correct. ObjectInputStream reads bytes from a stream and converts them back into objects using readObject().
ObjectDeserializer does not exist in the standard Java API.
File does not have a readObject() method.
